title: The Power of the Sacred Living Letters: The Kabbalah Book of Change
summary: A spiritual guidebook co-authored by Judith Orloff and Jasmyne Boswell that presents each of the 22 Hebrew letters of the Alef-Bet as tools for personal transformation and self-discovery rooted in Kabbalistic teachings. Each letter chapter includes its meaning, numerical value, calendar connection, reflective questions, shadow aspects, and suggested "right actions." The book draws on Chassidic stories, Torah commentary, and teachings from figures like the Baal Shem Tov and various Rabbis to connect ancient Jewish mysticism with practical spiritual growth exercises.
authorship: Judith Orloff, M.Ed. and Jasmyne Boswell. The Authors Notes section (pages 81-83) includes personal reflections from both authors. Orloff describes herself as a spiritual guide, non-dual transpersonal therapist and author who co-designed programs with Lubavitch of Bucks County. Boswell describes her inspiration from Celtic Runes leading to a Kabbalistic exploration of the Hebrew Alphabet.

title: Dissertation Critique - Nowhere Man by Tracy John Skipp
summary: Judith Orloff's academic critique of Tracy John Skipp's 2010 doctoral dissertation "Nowhere Man: Autoethnographic Reflections on Identity, Family, and Leadership" for the ELC 727 Methods Action Research course with Dr. Anna DiStefano at Fielding Graduate University. Orloff evaluates Skipp's use of autoethnography to explore leadership intimacy, his identification with Saint Francis of Assisi, his struggle with Franciscan Roman Catholic values in a university administration setting, and his three-part framework of leadership as intimacy with self, others, and developmental intimacy. The critique addresses the study's framing concepts (personalism, intimacy, fatherhood), research methods (360 assessment, interviews, reflective journaling), and data collection challenges.
authorship: Judith Orloff. Written for ELC 727 Methods Action Research course, submitted 3/11/17. Instructor: Dr. Anna DiStefano, Fielding Graduate University. The dissertation being critiqued is by Tracy John Skipp (Educational Leadership, 2010).

title: Insight as a Core Mechanism of Mindfulness: An Action Research Project
summary: An action research project by Judith Orloff at Fielding Graduate University investigating whether insight is a core mechanism of mindfulness practice. The paper distinguishes between Western (conceptual, Jon Kabat-Zinn) and Eastern (Buddhist, non-conceptual) mindfulness approaches, focusing on the latter. It proposes a study with 20 participants using narrative inquiry methodology, including in-depth interviews, a 28-day daily email survey with four-question assessments, and focus group exit interviews. The research questions examine whether being insightful leads to deeper mindfulness, whether insight leads to beneficial behavior, and whether insight reduces blame through reduced projection. Includes a 63-question autobiography questionnaire, mobile app mockups from Orloff's organization Radical Choices, Inc., and references to her six principles of mindfulness.
authorship: Judith Orloff, Fielding Graduate University. References her organization Radical Choices, Inc. and the app DeepSee. Mentions collaboration with Doubleday (Orloff & Doubleday 2015). The paper engages with work by Jon Kabat-Zinn, Ellen Langer, Chade meng Tan, Valerie Bentz, Peter Fenner, and Bessel van der Kolk.

title: Dissolving Adverse Childhood Conditioning through a Mindfulness Curriculum for Parents and Children from Preschool through High School

She describes 45 years of exploring methodologies to dissolve negative childhood conditioning, references the concept of 'trance state' from Four Arrows, and discusses her plan to use Phenomenology as her dissertation methodology. The document also mentions her intent to explore Theories of Change with Montessori early childhood education for Nicola's class. References include Thomas Verny's 'The Secret Life of the Unborn Child' and Frederick Leboyer's 'Birth without Violence.'
authorship: Judith Orloff. Written as Assignment 3 for ELC-721-17SPI course, submitted to Lee Mahon on February 15, 2017, at Fielding Graduate University.

Includes extended time options such as 'Gloves of Arthritis' (disability simulation), trust walks, and 'Being Disabled' imagination exercises. Contains assumptions, time estimates (147 hours total), and investment estimates ($5,000 for design/development, $500-$1,000 per center).
authorship: Orloff Consulting 2004 (Judith Orloff). Handwritten notes on cover reference '25 minute pres. with 3 add ons' and 'people to interview at their end, 5 of each: teenager & kids.'

authorship: Friendship Circle (Rabbi Zalman Grossbaum, Executive Director, Livingston, NJ). Orloff Consulting of Boulder, Colorado enlisted to create the workshop.

title: Letter from the Rebbe on the Care and Education of Jewish Children with Disabilities
summary: A letter from the Lubavitcher Rebbe dated 22 Av, 5739 (1979), responding to a request for his views on the care and education of Jewish children with intellectual disabilities. The Rebbe provides detailed guidelines including: treating each case individually rather than applying group rules, starting from the premise that disabilities are temporary and improvable, avoiding exaggerated expectations while giving guarded encouragement, involving trainees in leadership roles, addressing the controversy around 'group homes' with a recommendation for individual evaluation, emphasizing the importance of Jewish education and identity for children with disabilities (not treating it as a secondary concern), and the therapeutic value of religious observance and community belonging. The letter closes with reference to the Lubavitch principle of 'Ve'ohavta Lereacha Kamocha' (Love your fellow as yourself) and a blessing to the recipient in their capacity as Regional Chairman of the Council For Mental Retardation.
authorship: The Lubavitcher Rebbe (Menachem Mendel Schneerson, implied by title 'The Rebbe Writes' and Lubavitch reference)

title: Assessment of Montessori Teacher Training Using Theories of Change
summary: An academic paper by Judith Orloff for the ELC-726 Theories of Change course at Fielding Graduate University examining how Theory of Change (TOC) frameworks can be applied to assess Montessori teacher training programs. The paper explores the Montessori emphasis on teacher self-awareness, non-judgmental observation, and self-assessment, and argues these align well with TOC methodology. It includes an interview with Ann Velasco, Director of Training at the Southwest Institute for Montessori Studies, a five-step TOC framework for teacher assessment, and references to Fritjof Capra's concept of paradigm. Appendices include a cartoon, Orloff's original 21-element Model for Change (developed in 2001 as CEO of Educational Discoveries), an illustrated Model for Change diagram, and a Championing Change Activity Feedback Form.
authorship: Judith Orloff, M.Ed. Written for ELC-726: Theories of Change course at Fielding Graduate University. References her prior work as CEO of Educational Discoveries, a leadership and development company. Includes interview data from Ann Velasco, Director of Training at Southwest Institute for Montessori Studies.

title: Sources of Information - Head, Heart, and Soul (Chapter 10)
summary: Chapter 10 from a larger book exploring six sources of information available for decision-making: three internal (head, heart, and soul) and three external (support from others, mass consciousness, and universal consciousness). The chapter explains how the "head" operates from past programming and belief systems, the "heart" provides present-moment emotional information, and the "soul" reveals core values and life purpose. It includes interactive exercises comparing head vs. heart responses, discusses true guilt vs. false guilt, the role of support in personal change, and introduces universal consciousness as a source of intuition and knowing. Personal anecdotes from Peg and Judith illustrate the concepts, including stories about marriage, relationships, and trusting intuition.

title: The 7-11 Game - Ethics and Choices Role Play Exercise
summary: A role-play exercise designed for use in the Choices or Learning Choices program. Participants play teenagers (about age 14) who have witnessed a respected classmate (the class president) rob a 7-11 store and knock down an elderly lady. They adopt assigned personality roles (Thief, Liberal, Moral, Peacemaker, Fair) and role-play a group conversation confronting the classmate. The exercise includes an optional guided meditation that projects participants forward in time at 10, 20, 40, and 50 year intervals to examine the long-term consequences of their choices on relationships, career, self-respect, and feelings about death. Concludes with sharing and the option to play the song "In a Simple Way."
authorship: No specific author credited. Created as part of the Choices / Learning Choices curriculum, associated with Judith Orloff's programs.

title: Learning Choices - Crossing the Abyss Game
summary: A team-building exercise from the Learning Choices program where participants simulate climbing Mount Learning to 10,000 feet. Teams of participants must cross a taped "abyss" on the floor using only three mats as stepping surfaces, with no talking allowed during the climb. The exercise is designed to demonstrate integrity, personal responsibility, teamwork, congruence, and how people respond to moment-to-moment conditions in a group setting. Includes detailed setup instructions (5ft by 20ft taped squares), five rules for the game, and a structured debrief with discussion questions about commitment, teamwork, assumed roles, success, and helping other teams.
authorship: No specific author credited. Created as part of the Learning Choices curriculum, headed "Learning Choices" at the top of each page.

title: Mom and Dad Game - Parental Identity Exercise
summary: A 30-minute role-play exercise where participants embody their parents to explore inherited beliefs and patterns. In step one, participants become their same-sex parent at age 20, speaking about love, sex, marriage, children, money, work, power, intimacy, and success. In step two, they become that parent at their current age discussing the same topics. In step three, they switch to become their opposite-sex parent. The worksheet includes reflection prompts asking "How are you like your Mother?" and "How are you like your Father?" A handwritten note in red asks "Is this for everyone? Or just kids?" suggesting it was used across different program audiences.
authorship: No specific author credited. Associated with Judith Orloff's Choices program curriculum. Contains a handwritten editorial note in red ink.

title: Universe Game - Synergy and Heart's Desire Exercise
summary: An instructor's outline for the "Universe Game," a group exercise created by Choices International in 1988. The outline covers a 45-minute opening that includes defining synergy (the whole is greater than the sum), examples of synergy in families, bodies, nature, and companies, and defining heart's desire as what you really want versus what you think you want. It details when the Universe (facilitator) issues fines (visible fighting, lack of synergy, desperation, losing heart's desire after getting it) and rewards (genuine giving, demonstrated synergy, asking for something).
authorship: Choices International, 1988. The footer on both content pages reads "Choices International, 1988."

Includes their symbolic attributes, compass directions, colors, seasons, and types of spells each element governs.

title: "The Global Brain" by Peter Russell (Excerpt - Chapter 1: The Blue Pearl)

It then presents James Lovelock's Gaia Hypothesis, which proposes that Earth functions as a self-regulating living system, detailing evidence including the stability of surface temperature over millions of years, ocean salt concentration remaining at 3.4%, atmospheric oxygen stabilized at 21%, ammonia levels neutralizing acid rain, and the ozone layer protecting DNA. The chapter argues that these homeostatic mechanisms suggest the planet behaves as a single living organism rather than operating through coincidence.
authorship: Peter Russell. This is an excerpt from his published book "The Global Brain." The document appears to be a photocopy or scan of the printed book pages (pages 17-26 in the original book numbering).

summary: Draft instructor's manual for the Extended Teaching Program (ETP), an 8-session personal responsibility training curriculum created by Quantum Educational Discoveries, Inc. (copyright 1991, revised 04/23/91). Each session spans a multi-day weekend format and covers: owning personal history, living from personal responsibility, integrating the primary family (including a "Mom and Dad Game" and projection exercises), vision and power (with a vision quest and purpose meditation), creating adult relationships (with "schiz-skits" demonstrations), sex/bodies/physical integration (as a retreat with body autobiographies and tantric sexuality discussion), personal integrity (with a "Truth or Consequences" questionnaire), and mastering the process of change. The manual includes detailed instructor notes on facilitation techniques, group exercises, partner work, family day logistics, reading assignments (Richard Bach's "Illusions," Jane Roberts' Seth books, Stephen King's "The Talisman," Bernie Siegel, Buckminster Fuller), and curated music selections to close each session. References to Judith Orloff appear in Session 8 notes.
authorship: Quantum Educational Discoveries, Inc. (QED). No individual author is named on the document, but the final session notes reference Judith (likely Judith Orloff) as someone participants send assignments to, and include personal anecdotes about Judith. The program appears to be an extension of the Choices Weekend created by QED.

title: Graduate Training Outline - Choices Weekend Follow-up
summary: An instructor's guide for a 6-week follow-up program designed for graduates of the Choices Weekend seminar, published by QED (Quantum Educational Discoveries) in 1990. The program meets three hours weekly in a residential setting with 8-12 participants at $375 per person. It outlines six sessions covering Connection, Model for Change and Reaction, Projection, Responsibility and Integrity (Parts I and II), and a final Demonstration session, each with specific exercises such as partner role-play for projection, values identification on flip charts, and a personal change project that participants track throughout the six weeks.
authorship: Published by QED, Inc. (Quantum Educational Discoveries), P.O. Box 918, Williston, Vermont 05495. Copyright 1990. Dated 12/11/90. No individual author named.

title: The Choices Weekend - Instructor's Manual
summary: The complete instructor's manual for The Choices Weekend, a three-day personal development seminar created by Judith Orloff-Falk and Peg Doubleday and published by Educational Discoveries (QED). The manual provides a detailed hour-by-hour program outline across three days with specific teaching scripts, guided meditations, exercises, poster diagrams, and music cues. Day One covers belief systems, the Bliss/Now model of how sensations become feelings and beliefs, reactions as cover-ups, and the 7-11 Question Game. Day Two teaches the Seven Steps to Get Out of Reaction, personal responsibility, unconditional love, control as fear of loss, intimacy versus 'into-me-see,' projection, and handling projections in five steps. Day Three covers vision quests, the Model for Change (an 8-step diagram from Conscious Choice through Resistance, Illusion/Chaos, Acknowledgment, Breakthrough, to Vision), and closes with action planning and a 'Recipe for Ecstatic Sex.' Includes a music guide listing 28 songs with their emotional purposes.
authorship: Copyright 1992 by Educational Discoveries (QED). Revised 12/4/91 and 1/9/92 by 'ch.' The creators of the course are identified within the text as Judith Orloff-Falk and Peg Doubleday. A handwritten annotation on page 16 reads 'Judy Care' (likely Judith Orloff-Falk's married name or note).

title: Natural Leadership: A Core Competency of Clarity
summary: A guidebook published by the Radical Love Foundation presenting Judith Orloff's "Natural Leadership" methodology, which frames clarity as the essential core competency for effective leadership. The document defines six guiding principles: Personal Responsibility, Sharing Direct Experience, Knowing Yourself, Honoring Our Word, Being Authentic, and Applying Skillful Means, each broken into specific sub-competencies with stated benefits. Developed over 30 years of organizational participation, it positions Natural Leadership as an innate ability to do the right thing when informed by clarity, authenticity, and natural ethics.
authorship: Judith Orloff, M.Ed. and the Radical Love Design Team. Published by Radical Love Foundation, Boulder, Colorado. Version dated June 16, 2013.

title: Awakened Relationships: A Core Competency of Unconditional Love
summary: A workbook published by the Radical Love Foundation (co-founded by Judith Orloff and Melissa Stuart) that defines and teaches the concept of "Awakened Relationships" through six guiding principles: Personal Response-Ability, Sharing Direct Experience, Being Authentic, Knowing Yourself, Honoring Our Word, and Applying Skillful Means. Each principle is presented with key tenets, benefits, and accompanying "Notes and Reflections" pages for the reader's personal journaling, along with a central diagram showing how the six competencies interconnect around themes of clarity, integrity, oneness, synergy, and natural wisdom.
authorship: Judith Orloff and the Radical Love Design Team, published by Radical Love Foundation, version September 7, 2013

title: VICI Opening Ceremony Speech - "In Praise of Venture" by Sister Elizabeth Candon
summary: A speech delivered on September 29, 1973 at the opening ceremony of the Vermont Institute of Community Involvement (VICI) by Sister Elizabeth Candon, President of Trinity College in Burlington, Vermont. The speech, titled "In Praise of Venture," celebrates VICI as a new educational institution that emphasizes community-based learning, drawing on Milton's Paradise Lost, T.S. Eliot, George B. Leonard, Arnold Toynbee, Phillip Boxxerman, and William Faulkner's Nobel Prize acceptance speech. Candon praises VICI's innovative approach to education through community involvement and experiential learning while also affirming the value of traditional institutions.
authorship: Sister Elizabeth Candon, President of Trinity College, Burlington, Vermont. The speech was delivered at the VICI Opening Ceremony and Festival on September 29, 1973. VICI was founded by Dr. Steward LaCasce, who is referenced throughout.

title: Burlington College Convocation - Judith Orloff's Schedule, Speech, and Research Notes (2015)
summary: Materials from Judith's appearance at the Burlington College Convocation on September 9, 2015. Includes her day schedule (executive team meeting, media interviews with VPR and WCAX, trustee meeting, reception), bullet-point speech notes reflecting on co-founding Burlington College in 1972 with Stuart LaCasce and the social movements that shaped their generation (environmentalism, feminism, LGBT rights, civil rights), and background research notes on John Dewey's educational philosophy and Debra Meyerson's concept of 'tempered radicalism' as a model for incremental change from within institutions.
authorship: Speech notes written by Judith Orloff. Schedule prepared by staff (footer: 'LB Corres CM'). Research notes likely compiled by Judith or an assistant as preparation material.

title: Correspondence with W. Edwards Deming (1992)
summary: Correspondence between Judith Orloff-Falk and W. Edwards Deming in early 1992. Includes Judith's first letter (January 23, 1992) on Educational Discoveries letterhead introducing herself after attending Deming's seminar in San Jose, describing her consulting work with Wilcox Memorial Hospital in Kauai, Hawaii (with partner John Dowd) on driving out fear and building constancy of purpose, and enclosing a copy of "Choices for Success." Then Deming's personal reply (February 14, 1992) praising her book as "great," expressing his desire to spend time with her, and inviting her criticism and extension of his 4-day seminar content and his forthcoming book "The New Economics." Finally, Judith's follow-up letter (February 27, 1992) responding to Deming's reply, discussing Japanese vs. American management consciousness, and reporting on their work transforming the culture at Wilcox Memorial Hospital from competition and blame to personal responsibility.
authorship: Judith Orloff-Falk, Vice President, Educational Discoveries (2511 55th Street, Boulder, CO 80301), and W. Edwards Deming, Ph.D., Consultant in Statistical Studies (4924 Butterworth Place, Washington 20016). Partner Peg Doubleday is also mentioned in Judith's letters.

title: Radical Love Foundation - Workshop Materials, Conference Proposals, Teaching Content, and Bios
summary: A compilation of Radical Love Foundation materials by Judith Orloff and co-founder Melissa Stuart, including workshop descriptions, conference proposals (notably for the Science and Nonduality Conference 2010 in San Rafael, California), core teaching content on topics like "Pure Inseeing," "Pure Listening," and "Pure Speaking," email correspondence with conference organizers, the Practicum Principles one-sheet, the Foundation's Purpose/Vision/Mission statement, detailed workshop outlines covering conditioning, unconditioned awareness, family systems, and archetypes, plus professional bios for both Judith and Melissa.
authorship: Written and compiled by Judith Orloff, M.Ed., with contributions from Melissa Stuart, M.A., and email correspondence from Alexa Cloud and Salina Storozuk. Created for internal use by the Radical Love Foundation team and for conference submissions.

title: Radical Love Foundation - The Future of Executive Leadership Development
summary: A slide presentation from the Radical Love Foundation (copyright 2013) on the future of executive leadership development. Critiques the present state of leadership education for ignoring the 'shadow of the leader,' relying on projection and judgment, using linear competencies, and approaching change with fear. Identifies systemic problems including discomfort with responsibility without empowerment, inadequate feedback methodology, focus on output over outcome, and emotional intelligence not being easily learned or modeled. Envisions a future where authentic relationships and natural leadership competencies thrive, emotional literacy skills are as important as reading, community connection is valued, and clarity, experiential learning, Radical Listening, and Radical Speaking are mainstays.
authorship: Radical Love Foundation, copyright 2013. Developed from relationships with Bank of America, Fleet BankBoston, Midas, Johnson & Johnson, and other Fortune 500 executives.

title: Book Outline - Radical Love: Awakened Relationships and Natural Leadership
summary: A detailed book outline dated 12/18/2013 for 'Radical Love: Awakened Relationships and Natural Leadership' by Judith Orloff and Melissa (co-founders of the Radical Love Foundation). The book is structured in five parts across ten chapters, built around six guiding principles: Personal Responsibility, Knowing Our Self, Being Authentic, Honoring Our Word, Sharing Direct Experience, and Applying Skillful Means. Each chapter includes stories, exercises, and meditations designed to help readers develop awakened relationships and natural leadership through dissolving conditioned responses and living with clarity and authenticity.
authorship: Co-authored by Judith Orloff and Melissa (last name not specified). The file path references 'C:\Users\Alexa\Documents\00 NewRadical Books\Book Outline18Dec13v2.docx', suggesting Alexa may have been involved in document preparation. The outline notes their seven-year collaboration and study leading to the Radical Love Foundation.

title: The Choices Weekend - Personal Discovery Form
summary: A multi-page intake questionnaire given to participants before The Choices Weekend seminar. The form collects extensive personal history including birth circumstances (planned, wanted, birth complications, twin, premature, breech, caesarean), family dynamics (parents' relationship, divorce, siblings, deaths), childhood experiences (illnesses, injuries, emotional traumas), sexual and reproductive history (separate sections for women and men covering pregnancies, miscarriages, abortions), current health status (illnesses, injuries, medications, psychiatric care, allergies, surgeries), personal psychology (desires, fears, self-perception, thoughts about life and relationships), previous workshop experience, and emergency contact information. Participants are asked to bring the completed form to the Weekend.
authorship: No author or publisher credited on the form itself. Based on its title 'The Choices Weekend Personal Discovery Form,' it was created by the same organization (QED / Educational Discoveries) that produced the Choices Weekend program, founded by Judith Orloff-Falk and Peg Doubleday.

title: Radical Choices - Leadership in Recovery Day Two Workbook
summary: Day Two participant workbook for the Radical Choices "Leadership in Recovery" program using Disruptive Learning Technology (DLT), copyright 2015. Focuses on removing blocks to leadership through understanding the Reactive Self (automatic responses from the past), developing personal responsibility as 'response-ability,' recognizing reactions as pitfalls (judgment, interpretation, projection), dissolving reactions, cultivating authenticity, maintaining integrity, and applying the six DLT principles. Includes recovery-specific scene study activities set in addiction treatment facilities and a 'Cleaning Up The Mess' integrity self-assessment exercise.
authorship: Ali Boaldin / Radical Choices LLC, copyright 2015 (contact: Office@radicalchoicesllc.com).

title: Radical Choices - Train the Trainer Certification Program, Session Three: "Beyond Suffering - The Naked Bald Truth"
summary: Session Three participant workbook for the Radical Choices Disruptive Learning Technology (DLT) Train the Trainer Certification Program, copyright 2016, subtitled 'Beyond Suffering: The Naked Bald Truth.' This is a three-day intensive designed to prepare trainers to take DLT into the world through relationships, work, and interactions. Day One ('Know What Is / Own What Is') features a provocative mock trial activity where God/Great Spirit/Unconditioned is put on trial for crimes against humanity, explores nondual awareness vs. conditioned experience using Peter Fenner's framework, examines how mental 'pictures' and personal Greek tragedy 'fatal flaws' shape our lives, and introduces Being vs. Doing through e.e. cummings poetry. Day Two ('Clarity') includes live DLT demonstrations by Judith, Jungian archetypes in literature (Hero, Mother, Innocent Youth, Magician, Doppelganger, Scapegoat, Villain), and a 'Speakable Me' activity for sharing reactive states without judgment. Day Three ('Taking It Out In The World') covers organizational DLT demos, Clear Mind practice, and Awakened Action presentations on escaping mass consciousness conditioning.
authorship: Judith Orloff / Ali Boaldin / Radical Choices LLC, copyright 2016. Marked 'CONFIDENTIAL - This workbook is the confidential intellectual property of Radical Choices, LLC - DO NOT DISSEMINATE.' Nondual Awareness diagram credited to Peter Fenner.

title: The Inward Bound Institute Proposal - "Touching Reality" Series (Fragment)
summary: A single-page fragment from a proposal by Orloff Learning, Inc. for 'The Inward Bound Institute' and its 'Touching Reality' series. The document describes Rabbi Yehuda Shemtov of the Glazer Center in Yardley, PA, and his innovative educational programming that combines ancient Kabbalistic sources with modern learning applications such as self-discovery, accelerative learning, and emotional intelligence. The proposal describes Shemtov's mission to share the teachings of Chassidic tradition and Kabbalah through a new learning methodology, seeking financial partners for world-wide programs. Dated 2006.
authorship: Orloff Learning, Inc. (Judith Orloff's company). Written in support of Rabbi Yehuda Shemtov's programs.

title: Radical Love Foundation - Readings, Poems, and Workshop Teaching Materials
summary: A collection of teaching materials used in Radical Love Foundation workshops, copyright 2011. Includes the parable "Now" about a monk's urgency for presence, the poem "The Kama Sutra of Kindness: Position Number 3" by Mary Mackey, W.N. Murray's "Commitment" passage from The Scottish Himalayan Expedition, a section on emotions as waves of energy referencing Dr. Candace Pert's "Molecules of Emotion," teachings on the reactive self and conditioning, Prigogine's dissipative structures applied to learning, integrity patterns and pitfalls, negative bonding, a "Living the Future Now" Winter 2012 program description ($1500 tuition), a poem by Guthema Roba, and a Rumi poem translated by Nader Khalili.
authorship: Radical Love Foundation (RLF), copyright 2011. Teaching materials compiled by Judith Orloff and associates. Includes works by Mary Mackey, W.N. Murray, Candace Pert (referenced), Guthema Roba, Rumi (translated by Nader Khalili), and Karlfried Graf von Durkheim.

title: Radical Love Participant Workbook
summary: A participant workbook for the Radical Love program containing interactive exercises, journaling pages, and teaching content organized around core concepts. Includes "The Choice of Love" poem contrasting fear and love, exercises on introduction and deepest desires, the "Birth to Now" timeline exercise, teachings on the Reactive/Simulated Self and childhood conditioning (with extensive handwritten annotations), "Feelings not Experienced... Persist and Control You" diagrams, the "Mom and Dad Game" role-play exercise, "Approval and Disapproval Fantasy," "True Desire" mortality exercise, a memorial service eulogy-writing exercise, an excerpt from Karlfried Graf von Durkheim's "The Way of Transformation," and the "Commitment" passage by W.N. Murray.
authorship: Radical Love Foundation / Judith Orloff. Contains extensive handwritten annotations and edits throughout (particularly on the Reactive Self pages, suggesting revision from 'Reactive Self' to 'Simulated Self'). Includes excerpted works by Karlfried Graf von Durkheim and W.N. Murray.

title: Business & You - Seminar Participant Workbook
summary: A 76-page participant workbook for the "Business & You" seminar held November 7-9, 1997, a three-day experiential corporate training program rooted in Marshall Thurber's "Money and You" seminar. The workbook guides participants through interactive exercises, games, and frameworks covering learning levels (Dreyfus model), cognitive filters, emotional competency, trust, commitment management, coordinating action workflows (Fernando Flores), the Knower vs. Learner paradigm (Fred Kofman), Buckminster Fuller's principles of integrity and precession, and wealth-building strategies. It was customized for The Neenan Company, a DesignBuild firm, and includes their "Rules of the Game" corporate values document alongside extensive fill-in-the-blank note pages and a recommended reading list of over 100 titles.
authorship: Created by Business & You Seminars (copyright 1996), evolved from Marshall Thurber's original "Money and You" seminar. Draws on frameworks by Fred Kofman, Fernando Flores, Rafael Echeverria, H. Dreyfus, and Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi. Customized for delivery at The Neenan Company. Judith Orloff participated in this seminar as part of her corporate leadership education.

title: The Art & Science of Mindful Living - Participant Workbook
summary: A comprehensive multi-week participant workbook for 'The Art & Science of Mindful Living' program by the Radical Love Foundation. Organized into at least 7 weekly sessions covering Context (choosing love vs. fear, the F.A.V.O.R. method for empathic communication, context vs. content in communication, recipes for setting context), Insight (emotions as energy waves, shadow work, childhood reflection, true desire exercises, the DeepSee app), Personal Responsibility toward self (projection, judgment, dishonesty exercises), Personal Responsibility toward others (making amends, radical listening adapted from Peter Fenner, right action), Authenticity (reactive vs. authentic sharing, role-play 'Jumping Paradigms' exercise with homeless vet scenario in Boulder), and Integrity/Lying (cleaning up the mess of dishonesty). Each week includes self-assessment forms, interim assignments with the DeepSee app, journaling pages, and partner-sharing exercises. Includes poems by e.e. cummings and Bette Midler's 'The Rose,' quotes from Werner Erhard and Michael C. Jensen, Rumi via Coleman Barks, and the W.N. Murray commitment passage.
authorship: Radical Love Foundation / Judith Orloff. The workbook incorporates teachings adapted from Peter Fenner, quotes from Werner Erhard, Michael C. Jensen (HBS professor), W.N. Murray, and poems by e.e. cummings and Bette Midler. References the DeepSee app as a companion tool.

title: The End of Your World - Adyashanti Interview Transcript (Sounds True)
summary: A 19-page transcript of an in-depth interview between Sounds True publisher Tami Simon and spiritual teacher Adyashanti, excerpted from his book 'The End of Your World.' Topics covered include the nature of spiritual awakening as a change of perspective rather than a blissful state, the distinction between nonabiding and abiding awakening using the 'rocket ship' metaphor, the mystery of what fuels awakening, 'Velcro thoughts' and the narrowing gap between thought and seeing through it, pure feeling vs. thought-derived emotion, the gut as an intuitive sense organ, pure anger from an undivided state, the ego co-opting awakening into missionary zeal, the dangers of spiritual inflation, the inner voice as guide vs. superego, finding one's own way rather than relying on a teacher or tradition, his experience of 'final awakening' at age 32 including seeing past lives, death as the next experience of consciousness, and his teaching that 'waking up is dying.' Includes handwritten annotations throughout marking key passages.
authorship: Interview conducted by Tami Simon (Sounds True publisher) with Adyashanti. Excerpted from the book 'The End of Your World' published by Sounds True. The document includes handwritten annotations (likely by Judith Orloff or a Radical Love Foundation reader) marking passages about secondary thought patterns, pure emotions vs. duplications of thinking, and pure anger.

title: Applying Accelerated Learning to Course Design - Training Workbook
summary: A comprehensive training workbook produced by Educational Discoveries that teaches instructional designers how to apply accelerated learning principles to course design. Presents the proprietary "Whole Being Model for Teaching and Learning" integrating mind, body, heart, and spirit. Includes a complete copy of The Accounting Game (copyright 1983), the Choices International Model for Change (copyright 1990), a learning styles inventory based on the 4MAT system, and reference materials on brain research, dissipative structures, and Deming's quality principles applied to education.
authorship: Created by Educational Discoveries (co-founded by Judith Orloff). Compiles proprietary frameworks alongside licensed third-party materials: The Accounting Game (1983), Choices Paradigm for Change (1990), 4MAT System by Bernice McCarthy, brain research from Tony Buzan, and a 1990 article by Lewis A. Rhodes on Deming. Mind maps credited to Rob Evans.

title: The Accounting Game - Book Publishing Documents
summary: A collection of materials related to the publication of "The Accounting Game" book by Educational Discoveries (EDI) and Sourcebooks. It includes a draft foreword explaining the accelerative learning methodology behind the book, a press release announcing the joint venture between EDI and Source Books with co-authors Darrell Mullis and CEO Judith Orloff, and email correspondence from March 1998 between Larry Bograd and Todd Stocke at Sourcebooks regarding author credit order.
authorship: Compiled materials involving Judith Orloff (CEO of EDI), Larry Bograd (EDI's legal/business representative), Todd Stocke (Managing Editor at Sourcebooks), and Darrell Mullis (EDI's top presenter and co-author).

title: Fielding Graduate University EdD Application
summary: Judith Orloff's application materials for the EdD program at Fielding Graduate University, including a Statement of Purpose and a Self-Reflective Essay dated June 2, 2016. The Statement of Purpose describes her pursuit of Disruptive Learning Technology (DLT), a patent-pending process with an app called DeepSee in the Apple Store, designed to help children transcend childhood conditioning. The Reflective Essay traces her professional journey from meeting Dr. Steward LaCasce at the University of Pennsylvania in 1971, co-founding the Vermont Institute of Community Involvement (VICI, later Burlington College), creating the Noogenesis program at Shelburne Farms, working as a psychotherapist, and developing her methodology over 40+ years. It also includes a professional resume listing roles at Horizon House, University of Pennsylvania, Burlington College, Carriage House Associates in Health, Choices International, Educational Discoveries, and Orloff Learning/Real Impact Learning.
authorship: Judith Orloff (applicant ID 3964194). Written for Fielding Graduate University EdD application. The reflective essay references Dr. Steward LaCasce, Carol Moore (President of Burlington College), and various collaborators throughout her career.

title: WHY's Guide to the Human Side of CPR - Complete Training Program
summary: A comprehensive four-day corporate training seminar workbook created for Cargill, designed to teach the human and emotional side of CPR (Corporate Process Reengineering/Change). The program includes multiple interactive modules: "The Chronicles of WHY" (a narrative role-playing exercise set aboard the S.S. Destiny), "WHY: A Game of Integrity" (a commodity trading simulation with play money and role cards), "The Synergy Game" (a non-verbal communication exercise), and concluding sections on consultant tools, action planning, and stress relief. Includes custom watercolor cover art, printable game materials (play money branded "The World of WHY" with "In Each Other We Trust"), and structured reflection worksheets.
authorship: Created by Judith Orloff as part of her corporate consulting practice. Designed for Cargill employees undergoing a major CPR (change/reengineering) initiative. References the Seven C's Consulting Model and the FAVOR Method as proprietary frameworks.

title: Secrets - Presentation Visual Notes (May 1984)
summary: A set of 11 hand-drawn visual notes from a presentation called "Secrets" by Judith, dated May 1984. The illustrations use a visual facilitation style to capture key concepts including: presence vs. content, Buckminster Fuller's last lecture, choice and reaction, addictions as unexperienced experiences, duplication, integrity, judgement, getting gotten (being experienced), communication breakdowns (words 7%, voice 38%, body language 55%), the process of education referencing Prigogine, forgiveness (referencing Rev. Terry Cole-Whittaker), and presentation techniques like creating anticipation and using timers. References include Richard Bach's "Illusions" and Werner Erhard.
authorship: Judith Orloff (credited as 'Judith May 84' on the cover page)

title: Emotional Intelligence Project - Interview with Judith Orloff
summary: A 15-page transcript of a filmed interview with Judith Orloff for an Emotional Intelligence Project. Orloff discusses her preferred term "emotional literacy" over "emotional intelligence," defines it as the ability to be aware of internal experience and respond from that awareness. She addresses gender and cultural differences in emotional expression, how organizations like American Express, Bank of America, Fleet Bank, Midas International, Ford, and GM have adopted EI, and describes her company's approach of embedding EI into management training at three levels (beginning, functional, and business managers) rather than selling it as a standalone product. She discusses creating cognitive dissonance to drive real change, the role of franchise organizations in paradigm shifts, and implementation through web-based follow-up modules. She also covers resistance from HR professionals, the connection between emotional intelligence and workplace safety, and her belief that EI is both learned and remembered.
authorship: Judith Orloff (interviewee). Interviewer is unnamed. Produced as part of an Emotional Intelligence Project (appears to be a video/film production with offstage direction).

title: Conditioning's Last Stand - Integrity
summary: A brief two-page document consisting of a handwritten title page reading 'Conditioning's last stand - INTEGRITY' in pink marker, followed by a page describing an alternative information-communicative theory of brain organization covering neural circuits, holographic information distribution, memory storage, and quantum mechanisms of consciousness.
authorship: Handwritten title page likely by Judith Orloff. Scientific text excerpted from an academic paper on brain organization and information-communicative theory.

title: Radical Choices Leadership Programs - Learning Methodology Overview
summary: A single-page overview of the Radical Choices learning methodology, explaining how the programs link emotion, spiritual relevance, and intellectual content to participant experience through a combination of logical, emotional, and spiritual experiences, abstract concepts, physical experiences, and taking action. Notes that programs can be customized to organizations.
authorship: Radical Choices. No individual author credited.

title: The Accounting Game - Instructor Manual
summary: A comprehensive instructor manual for teaching "The Accounting Game," a full-day interactive seminar created by Educational Discoveries that teaches fundamental accounting concepts through a lemonade stand simulation. The manual provides word-for-word scripts and detailed stage directions across an Introduction, Level 1, and Level 2, guiding instructors through teaching balance sheets, income statements, assets, liabilities, owner's equity, accrual accounting, accounts receivable, accounts payable, retained earnings, and prepaid expenses using colored game pieces, props, and role-playing. The pedagogical approach emphasizes Accelerative Learning with whole-brain engagement, participation, permission to make mistakes, and multisensory engagement including music, breathing exercises, and physical movement.
authorship: Created by Educational Discoveries (copyright holder). Internal training document for certified instructors delivering The Accounting Game seminar. This copy has the name 'Darrell' handwritten on the cover, likely Darrell Mullis (co-author of the Accounting Game book). Judith Orloff was co-founder of Educational Discoveries.

title: The Accounting Game: Complete Instructor Manual (Levels I-VI)
summary: A comprehensive instructor manual for The Accounting Game, an experiential learning program developed by Educational Discoveries that teaches accounting and financial literacy through a lemonade stand simulation. The manual guides instructors through six progressive levels using a two-column "What You Do / What You Say" format, covering balance sheets, income statements, accrual vs. cash accounting, accounts receivable, retained earnings, depreciation, inventory management, and cash flow statements. The teaching methodology incorporates physical props, group exercises, affirmation cards, and a diploma ceremony.
authorship: Created by Judith Orloff and Educational Discoveries as a proprietary instructor training manual. Designed for certified instructors delivering The Accounting Game to corporate and adult education audiences.

title: Core Technology Programs - Train-The-Trainer (TTT) Workbook
summary: A Train-The-Trainer workbook created by Educational Discoveries, Inc. (dated 05.28.98) designed to teach instructors how to present accelerative learning seminars. The workbook covers neuroscience foundations including the Triune Brain Model (reptilian complex, limbic system, neocortex), right brain/left brain research by Professor Robert Ornstein and Dr. Paul MacLean, and instructor methodology concepts such as Setting the Context, the Instructor's Safety Net (Space, Enrollment, Common Ground, Gradient, Ritual, Discovery), Reaction and the "Stop, Look, Listen, Act" tool, the F.A.V.O.R. method for handling questions, and Giving and Receiving Support.
authorship: Created by Educational Discoveries, Inc., the corporate training company founded by Judith Orloff (President/CEO). Written for instructors being certified to deliver Educational Discoveries' accelerative learning programs.

title: The Nature of Conflict - Course Materials and Conflict Resolution Participant Workbook
summary: A comprehensive conflict resolution training package from Educational Discoveries, Inc. (part of the Provant Solution), combining a detailed course outline for an 8-hour program and a participant workbook. The course outline covers sources of conflict, personal responsibility, the Conflict Resolution Model, individual and team conflict resolution activities, and action planning. The participant workbook includes Tom Crum's "Magic of Conflict" philosophy, a step-by-step conflict resolution framework, and "The Model for Change" with its 10-step paradigm shift process and role-playing "Players" exercise.
authorship: Created by Educational Discoveries, Inc. (part of the Provant Solution), with Judith Orloff as President/CEO. Quotes Tom Crum's "Magic of Conflict." Written for individuals at all levels within large organizations.

title: The Model for Change - Supplementary Materials
summary: A collection of materials related to Educational Discoveries' proprietary "Model for Change" framework. It includes the cover page for "The Model for Change: Steps for Creating a Paradigm Shift in People," an excerpt from Chapter 11 of "Choices for Success: Your Happiness In Your Own Hands" laying out an 11-step process for navigating change, an "About Educational Discoveries" overview page, a colorful visual map of the change model cycle, and an introductory text describing the 10-step process.
authorship: Created by Educational Discoveries (EDI), based in Boulder, CO. Judith Orloff was president and CEO. The chapter excerpt comes from the book "Choices for Success: Your Happiness In Your Own Hands."

title: The Model for Change For Managers - Program Overview
summary: A program overview document for "The Model for Change For Managers," a two-day training program created by Educational Discoveries (copyright 2001, dated 10.12.01). The document outlines nine training modules across two days covering topics including paradigm shifts, the 8-step Model for Change, resistance vs. reaction, giving and receiving support, creating an environment for change, communication tools (the 6 Tools for Communicating and F.A.V.O.R.), the Synergy Game, and taking ownership for change. It also includes color-coded role-play scenario cards for improvisation activities featuring characters like Sulky Supervisor, Fresh as a Newborn Babe, Willing Worker, Wary Worker, and Marginal Manager.
authorship: Created by Educational Discoveries (noted as 'Part of the Provant Solution'). Judith Orloff was a co-founder of Educational Discoveries. Written for facilitators delivering the Model for Change program to managers of teams undergoing organizational change.

title: Breakthrough - Model for Change Participant Workbook
summary: A participant workbook for the 'Breakthrough' corporate leadership training program developed by Educational Discoveries (part of the Provant Solution). The workbook teaches the 'Model for Change,' a 10-step framework for navigating organizational and personal paradigm shifts, covering concepts like Response-Ability, Purpose, Mission, Vision, Objectives, Paradox, Reaction, Illusion, Crisis, Chaos of Creation, Perturbation, Congruence, and Synergy. It draws on thought leaders including Amir Levy and Uri Merry, Edward Simon, John D. Adams, Marilyn Ferguson, and Stephen Covey.
authorship: Created by Educational Discoveries (Part of the Provant Solution), co-founded by Judith Orloff. Copyright 2001, dated 10.12.01. Designed as a participant workbook for corporate leadership training programs.

title: Educational Discoveries - Conference, Press & Case Study Materials
summary: A compilation of press coverage, conference materials, and corporate case studies related to Educational Discoveries (EDI). It includes pages from the 2nd Annual Emotional Intelligence Summit program featuring speakers like Peter Salovey, Richard Boyatzis, David Whyte, and Judith Orloff. It also contains a Training Magazine article about EDI's work with Midas International on their culture change initiative, and detailed case studies of EDI's corporate training projects for Midas, Bank of America, Cablevision, and FleetBoston Financial.

title: Judith Orloff in the Daily Camera - Radical Love Foundation Press Coverage (2013)
summary: A three-page scan of newspaper coverage from the Boulder Daily Camera, dated Wednesday, January 9, 2013. authorship: Article by Aimee Heckel, Camera Staff Writer, published in the Boulder Daily Camera. Photos by Jessica Cuneo. The subject is Judith Orloff, founder of the Radical Love Foundation.

title: Using Nonduality to Ameliorate Early Childhood Trauma: An Autoethnography (Doctoral Dissertation, 2020)
summary: Judith Orloff's doctoral dissertation submitted to Fielding Graduate University for the degree of Doctor of Education, copyright 2020. The study is twofold: the first part explores how early childhood trauma (emotional, physical, or sexual) can define the course of a person's future, leading to both physical and psychiatric disease. The second part explores a gap in a foundational core therapeutic model that could be used universally with all modalities of therapy, proposing that nonduality, a Buddhist non-conceptual model of healing suffering, could ameliorate much of the trauma caused by abusive behavior. The dissertation uses autoethnography as its research method, telling the story of a woman in the second half of the 20th century who experienced postpartum depression and psychosis leading to misdiagnosis and inpatient psychiatric hospitalization, and how she achieved resilience and success through applying nonduality in coaching, therapeutic, and consultative practice. Chapter Four is an extended personal narrative covering Judith's childhood in Philadelphia, her parents' marriage, abuse and trauma from early childhood through adolescence, her time in New York City, psychiatric hospitalization, recovery through Horizon House, her work at the University of Pennsylvania, move to Vermont and founding of Burlington College (VICI), move to Colorado, and discovery of nonduality through Peter Fenner. Chapter Five presents conclusions, implications for practice, and her six-step 'Nonduality in Action' model. Committee chaired by Dr. Szabi Istai-Zee with members Anna M. DiStefano, Ira P. Glovinsky, Donna Farren, and Alan Davis.
authorship: Judith Orloff, EdD. Submitted to Fielding Graduate University in partial fulfillment of the requirements for the degree of Doctor of Education. Dissertation committee: Szabi Istai-Zee, PhD (Chair), Anna M. DiStefano, EdD (Research Faculty), Ira P. Glovinsky, PhD (Faculty Reader), Donna Farren (Student Reader), Alan Davis, PhD (External Examiner).
